subject: Dedicated capacity: cluster sizing & phased activation options
messages: Subject: Dedicated capacity: cluster sizing & phased activation options

Hi Emma —

Thanks for the meeting this morning. Per our discussion I put together three phased reservation options that map to the usage profile you shared (inference-heavy daytime loads, bursty batch jobs overnight). Attached: a one-page proposal and an XLS with ramp scenarios and cost run-rates.

High-level options (quick summary):
- Option A (Conservative): 24 min GPUs, 48 max GPUs over 9 months. Lower monthly commitment, higher burst pricing.
- Option B (Balanced): 48 min GPUs, 96 max GPUs over 6 months. Better unit cost, modest upfront commit.
- Option C (Aggressive): 96 min GPUs, 160 max GPUs over 3 months. Optimized for predictable latency at scale; best per-token economics.

Key operational notes:
- Warm pools: we recommend a 10–15% warm buffer on the min GPU count for steady-state latency SLAs.
- Pre-warm windows: 30–90 minute scheduled warm-ups for daily peak start times (configurable).
- Fallback routing: if dedicated capacity dips below min thresholds, requests automatically route to a compatible hosted variant (with prioritized throughput and fallbacks you control).

Next steps I propose: you review the attached spreadsheet and tell us which option most closely matches the internal runway you can commit to. If you want, we can draft a mutual action plan with milestone-based ramp triggers tied to usage thresholds.

Attachments: redwood-proposal-solarwave-v1.pdf, ramp-scenarios-2026.xlsx

Thanks — happy to hop on another call if helpful.

— Vivek

Vivek —

Thanks for the fast follow. Reviewing the sheet now — a couple quick clarifying items for us before we pick a lane:

1) Minimum GPUs: is the "min GPUs" a hard reservation (we're billed for all even if idle) or a guaranteed floor with short-term bursting above billed baseline? We need clarity for our CFO.
2) Warm buffer guidance — can that be expressed as a configurable policy so we only pay for the buffer during business hours?
3) Ramp triggers — we liked the milestone-based approach. Can you provide example metric thresholds and a sample timeline aligned with our Q3 product launch?

Also looping Ravi (ops) and procurement so we can surface any legal/procurement constraints early.

If it's easier, can Ben or Karthik put together a quick table that maps usage buckets to the three options (A/B/C) with monthly burn rates and expected per-token costs? We'll aim to pick a preferred option by EOD Friday.

— Emma

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity: cluster sizing & phased activation options

Emma / Ravi / procurement —

Thanks for the questions. Quick answers, plus I'm attaching a compact ramp table (ramp-scenarios-2026.xlsx) and a short appendix on security/networking.

1) Minimum GPUs: the min is a committed reservation. Billing covers the min count at the committed rate. That said, we offer a "soft buffer" policy you can enable which converts the warm buffer into a usage-based (pay-as-you-go) pool outside business hours — effectively reducing committed burn while preserving daytime latency. We list trade-offs in the spreadsheet.

2) Configurable buffer windows: yes. You can scope the warm buffer to specific cron windows (e.g., Mon–Fri 07:00–19:00 PT). Outside those windows the buffer becomes burstable capacity at standard hosted overage rates.

3) Ramp triggers: sample triggers we suggest (example - tie to 7-day trailing p95 QPS and cost-per-1k tokens):
   - Trigger 1 (activate tranche 1): sustained 7-day p95 > 1,200 QPS for 3 consecutive days OR usage growth > 18% week-over-week.
   - Trigger 2 (move to tranche 2): sustained 14-day p95 > 2,800 QPS OR sustained batch throughput exceeding nightly window by 2x for 10 nights.
   - Trigger 3 (full activation): forecasted monthly token consumption > 3.5B tokens or predictable spike events (marketing launch) confirmed.

Example mapped to our options (excerpt):
- Option A (24 -> 48): expected monthly cost: $82k -> $140k; warm buffer set to 10% business hours; pre-warm 45 minutes.
- Option B (48 -> 96): expected monthly cost: $150k -> $260k; warm buffer 12%; pre-warm 30 minutes; preferred for predictable PLG growth.
- Option C (96 -> 160): expected monthly cost: $270k -> $420k; warm buffer 15%; pre-warm 30 minutes; recommended if latency is absolute priority and you want aggressive unit price.

Operational safeguards we recommend adding to the MOU: automated rollback to hosted fallback, blackout windows for activation (we won't activate during major releases unless explicitly approved), and a 48–72 hour notice window for tranche activations to allow capacity warming.

Attachments: ramp-scenarios-2026.xlsx, network-security-sheet.pdf (infra appendix).

Happy to jump on a 30-min call tomorrow morning to walk through the spreadsheet line-by-line. Vivek / Karthik — can you both confirm availability?

Following up after Ben's note: if it helps the procurement review, we've drafted a short mutual action plan that ties activation tranches to both objective usage triggers (the ones Ben listed) and milestone-based credits if early ramp targets are missed. That keeps commercial alignment if the Q3 launch has variability.

Proposed immediate next steps:
1) You confirm preferred option (A/B/C) or ask us to propose a blended starter (e.g., start at Option B min but with Option A billing floor for first 60 days).
2) Procurement: if acceptable, I'll route a tailored term sheet and a DocuSign-ready MOU (link provided above).
3) Ops: Ben to run a 30-min session with Ravi and your infra team this week to validate pre-warm times and network security checklist.
